analysis: Examined all units. release-desktop.yml (lines 59, 519): the `source` and `publish` jobs moved from Blacksmith ubuntu to GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-24.04`. Permissions, artifact id/digest handoff, the source gate on master, and the secret-free build/package jobs are unchanged. No new secret exposure; the only change is where those jobs run. release-provider.yml: the same runner label change for resolve-env (source gate), qualify-sdk finalize, stage-release (R2 secrets) and register/publish (contents: write). A `timeout-minutes: 90` was added to the macOS build-and-release/signing job, so only availability is affected. Permissions and trust gates are not weakened in the supplied hunks, but I could not see the full jobs. release-dev-branch.yml: the push trigger was replaced by a 6-hour schedule plus `workflow_dispatch`. The `gate` job runs from master with `actions: write` and `contents: read`, no secrets, and no untrusted code. It only calls `gh workflow run --ref dev`, with a changed-file filter that fails open. The `dev` job is guarded by `workflow_dispatch && ref == refs/heads/dev`, so it signs already-on-dev code. Two things changed: any repo writer, not only ruleset-bypass accounts, can now trigger a Developer ID signing run of dev HEAD, and `cancel-in-progress` is now true (see finding). The old comment warning that `dev` needs a pull_request rule before it signs was removed, but the underlying review gap on dev is pre-existing. Remaining unknown: how the reusable publish/stage jobs behave when the parent run is cancelled mid-registration; that lives in release-provider.yml bodies not supplied. No provider runtime threat IDs (T-041 etc.) are touched.

findings.detail: The dev lane previously used `cancel-in-progress: false` with the note that a running run always completes. The head sets `cancel-in-progress: true` on group `release-dev-branch-dev`. The called release-provider.yml runs inside this caller's concurrency scope, so a second `workflow_dispatch` on `dev` cancels the whole in-flight run, including Developer ID signing, notarization, R2 staging and registration. Registration or staging can then be left half-finished, and each new run gets a new run_number version. Any repository writer can dispatch (no inputs, `github.ref == refs/heads/dev` is the only check) and can keep cancelling releases, or leave staged but unregistered artifacts. This replaces the push trigger, which only ledger-bypass accounts could fire. Fix: keep `cancel-in-progress: false` for the `dev` group, or cancel only before the signing and publish jobs. Restrict dispatch to authorized actors.
findings.title: Dev-branch signing/publish run can now be cancelled mid-flight by a later dispatch
